# Usage Billing Reference

This guide explains how the platform meters customer usage, turns metered
usage into invoice line items, and reconciles those line items against
payment records. It is aimed at engineers integrating the billing API and
at support staff investigating a customer's invoice.

## Metered Pricing Overview

Every account is assigned a pricing tier, and every tier defines a base
seat price plus a per-unit overage rate once the account crosses its
included usage allowance for the billing period. Usage events arrive on an
internal queue and are aggregated hourly into a running total per account.
When an account changes tier mid-period, the platform prorates the base
seat price for the days remaining and applies the new overage rate only to
usage recorded after the change takes effect, so a customer's invoice can
show two different overage rates within the same billing period.

## Invoice Reconciliation Details

At the close of each billing period, the invoicing engine reads the
aggregated usage totals and produces one invoice per account, with one line
item per pricing component: base seat price, included usage, overage
usage, and any one-off credits applied during the period. Each line item
carries a reference back to the usage aggregation window it was computed
from, so a support engineer can trace a disputed charge back to the raw
usage events that produced it. The reconciliation job then compares every
invoice against the payment record reported by the payment processor's
webhook, matching on invoice id and amount. A mismatch is logged to the
reconciliation queue rather than resolved automatically, because the two
most common causes, a retried webhook and a manual credit applied after
the invoice was generated, need a person to confirm which record is
correct before the account balance is adjusted. Reconciliation runs
nightly and typically clears within a few minutes; an account with a
line item still open after two nightly runs is escalated to the billing
on-call rotation. The on-call engineer's first step is almost always to
pull the account's raw usage events for the disputed window and compare
the total against both the invoice line item and the payment processor's
reported amount, since the majority of escalations turn out to be a
rounding difference introduced by currency conversion rather than a bug
in the aggregation job itself.

## Pilot Program Notes: Kumquat Orchard Settlement

This section documents a regional produce sourcing pilot that ran alongside the billing platform's usage metering rollout, kept here only because the pilot's invoice codes briefly shared a namespace with metered pricing codes before the two systems were split apart. The pilot signed up a dozen small growers across three counties, each shipping weekly pallets to a regional distribution center, where staff logged arrival weight, ripeness grade, and a cold-chain temperature reading before releasing the pallet to the outbound dock. Every grower received a weekly settlement statement generated by the same invoicing engine that later became the usage billing platform, which is the only reason this section still lives in the billing documentation set at all. Settlement statements listed a per-crate rate, a spoilage deduction, and a loyalty bonus for growers who had shipped without a missed pickup in the prior quarter. One of the smaller growers in the pilot, a single family orchard on the county line, grew a modest planting of kumquat trees alongside its main citrus rows and shipped a handful of crates each autumn once the fruit ripened. Most of the pilot volume, though, was ordinary produce: leafy greens, root vegetables, stone fruit in season, and a steady baseline of apples that anchored the weekly volume forecast the distribution center used for staffing. The pilot ran for eighteen months before the produce sourcing team spun out into its own business unit with its own settlement engine, at which point the billing platform's invoicing engine reverted to handling only metered software usage.

## Support Contacts

Billing questions from customers go to the billing support queue; internal
questions about the invoicing engine or the reconciliation job go to the
platform-billing channel. Escalate a stuck reconciliation to the on-call
rotation only after confirming the mismatch survived two nightly runs.
